title: Lebanon vs Jordan: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: For those seeking raw, energetic cultural immersion, incredible food, and buzzing nightlife amidst ancient ruins and stunning coastlines, Lebanon is your pick, budget around $80-150 USD/day. categories.summary: Both offer world-class historical sites, but their appeal lies in different aspects, making them equally compelling depending on traveler preference.

categories.name: h2 id="food-scene">🍽️ Food Scene
categories.summary: Lebanon's culinary scene is more diverse, innovative, and widely celebrated, offering an incredible range from street food to fine dining.

categories.name: h2 id="nightlife-entertainment">🥂 Nightlife & Entertainment
categories.summary: Beirut is renowned as a regional nightlife hub, offering a far more vibrant and diverse array of bars, clubs, and entertainment options.

categories.name: h2 id="nature-scenery">⛰️ Nature & Scenery
categories.summary: Jordan boasts internationally renowned natural wonders like Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea, offering iconic and unique landscapes.

categories.name: h2 id="costs-budget">💸 Costs & Budget
categories.summary: Despite its economic challenges, Lebanon offers more opportunities for budget-conscious travelers, especially for food and local experiences, with lower major tourist site fees.

categories.name: h2 id="safety-stability">🛡️ Safety & Stability
categories.summary: Jordan offers a significantly higher degree of political stability and tourist safety, with well-established and secure travel routes.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-around">🚗 Getting Around
categories.summary: Jordan offers more reliable and comfortable public transportation options, safer roads, and easier self-driving for tourists.

categories.name: h2 id="beaches-coastline">🏖️ Beaches & Coastline
categories.summary: Lebanon offers a vast and diverse Mediterranean coastline with traditional swimming beaches, lively beach clubs, and historical harbors.

categories.name: h2 id="solo-travel-friendliness">🧍 Solo Travel Friendliness
categories.summary: Jordan's established tourist infrastructure, high level of safety, and welcoming atmosphere make it highly conducive to solo travel.

categories.name: h2 id="accommodation">🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: Both countries provide excellent and diverse accommodation options, from luxury to budget, with unique local experiences in each.

faq.question: Is it easy to combine Lebanon and Jordan in one trip?
faq.answer: Yes, it's quite feasible. A direct flight between Beirut (BEY) and Amman (AMM) is only about an hour long. Several airlines, like Middle East Airlines and Royal Jordanian, offer daily flights. You'll typically need at least 10-14 days to do both justice, allowing 5-7 days per country without rushing.

faq.question: What's the best time of year to visit both countries?
faq.answer: Spring (March-May) and Autumn (September-November) are ideal for both. The weather is pleasant, not too hot for exploring, and the landscapes are at their best. Summer (June-August) can be extremely hot, especially in Jordan's desert regions, while winter (December-February) can bring cold, rain, and even snow to mountainous areas of both countries.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lebanon or Jordan?
faq.answer: Visa requirements vary by nationality. Many nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival for Jordan, often at a cost (around 40 JOD). For Lebanon, many countries also qualify for a visa on arrival, typically free or for a small fee. Always check the latest visa policies with your respective embassy or consulate before traveling.

faq.question: Is English widely spoken in Lebanon and Jordan?
faq.answer: Yes, English is widely spoken in both countries, especially in tourist areas, hotels, and restaurants. In Lebanon, French is also commonly spoken due to historical ties. While Arabic is the official language in both, you'll generally have no trouble communicating in English.

faq.question: How do tipping customs differ between the two?
faq.answer: Tipping is appreciated in both countries. In restaurants, a 10% tip is standard if a service charge isn't included. For taxi drivers, rounding up the fare is common. For tour guides and hotel porters, a few dollars (USD or local equivalent) is customary, especially for good service. It's not mandatory but is a nice gesture.

faq.question: What are the main differences in attire for women travelers?
faq.answer: In Jordan, particularly outside Amman and at religious sites, modest dress (shoulders and knees covered) is advisable to show respect. In Lebanon, especially Beirut, dress codes are generally more liberal, similar to Europe, though modest attire is still recommended for religious sites. Always carry a scarf for mosque visits.

faq.question: Are credit cards widely accepted, or should I carry cash?
faq.answer: Major credit cards are accepted in hotels, larger restaurants, and shops in both countries. However, for smaller shops, street food, local taxis, and many guesthouses, cash is essential. It's always wise to carry a mix of small denominations in local currency (JOD in Jordan, USD in Lebanon) for daily expenses.

faq.question: What's the internet connectivity like in both countries?
faq.answer: Both countries have decent internet connectivity. Wi-Fi is readily available in most hotels, cafes, and restaurants. You can easily purchase local SIM cards at the airport or telecom stores (e.g., Alfa/Touch in Lebanon, Zain/Orange/Umniah in Jordan) for affordable data plans, ensuring you stay connected throughout your trip.
